To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we were able to determine the number of copies of the SMN1 and the SMN2 genes in 60 DNA samples derived from SMA suspected patients/carrier from different regions of our country.
we developed a probe based methodology to determine the copy number of SMN genes in patients with spinal muscular atrophy.
we developed a MLPA method to determine the number of copies of SMN1 gene and SMN2 gene, which are located in the 5q chromosome and are paralog genes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and validation of a new method to detect copy number variation in the SMN1 and the SMN2 gene in SMA patients/carriers.
the study of the SMN gene family and its application to the diagnosis of spinal muscular atrophy.
the study of the SMN1 and its paralog SMN1 gene.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the SMN2 copy number is not related to the clinical phenotype in SMA.
the MLPA assay is a reliable method for detecting SMN1 and/or SMN2 copy numbers in patients/carriers of spinal muscular atrophy.
MLPA can be used as a reliable method to determine the SMN1/SMN2 copy number in suspected patients/carriers and it is a valuable tool to be used for the follow-up of SMA patients.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MLPA is a useful tool to determine the SMN1 and the SMN2 gene copy numbers and to identify patients/carriers in a population with high incidence of consanguinity.
the SMN2 copy number was increased in 53% of the cases and that the SMN1 exon 7 and/or 8 copy number was reduced in 53% (heterozygous or homozygous deletions).
MLPA can accurately determine SMN1 copy number and SMN2 copy number.
The main takeaway from our work is that
MLPA is a reliable and accurate technique to distinguish between SMN1 and 2 genes and to determine the copy number of both genes in a single reaction.
the use of MLPA in a multiplex format allows the determination of the number of copies for both paralog genes, SMN1 and its copy, SMN2.
MLPA is a fast, simple and reliable technique to detect copy number variation in the SMN genes and can be applied for the diagnosis and prognosis of SMA.
